standard: All requested material parts, independently per answer. Grade the ruling, not support labels.

grades.question: How does each player prepare their ID and Voting cards, what happens to cards for unused colors, and how is the initial Gold Bar pool dealt?
grades.expected_answer: Stand a visible ID in your chosen color, take the matching Voting set, remove target cards for colors not playing, and retain your Ambush card. Put the Gold deck face down and deal four central Gold Bar cards with values hidden.
grades.observed_answer: Each player chooses a color and places their Player ID card upright in its plastic stand, visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that color on the backs, remove cards targeting colors not in play, and keep each player's own Ambush. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four cards face down to the center with values hidden.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: IDs upright in stands; remove cards targeting colors not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, values hidden.
grades.reason: Explicit upright stand and visible chosen-color ID, matching Voting cards, unused colors removed, own Ambush retained and hidden central4 deal.

grades.question: Is there a player-by-player voting turn order? When may a player change their face-down choice, and when are choices revealed?
grades.expected_answer: There is no turn order. Choices can change until reveal. Once everyone has chosen, all reveal simultaneously.
grades.observed_answer: There is no individual player-by-player turn order. Players may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and “reveal all choices simultaneously.”
grades.reason: Explicitly states no player turn order, changes until reveal, and simultaneous reveal after all have chosen.

grades.question: In a seven-player vote, Red receives three votes, Blue two and Green two. Is a four-vote majority necessary to make Red a Target? Explain the Target threshold.
grades.expected_answer: No majority is required: the greatest vote total determines the Target. Red alone is Target because three is the highest count.
grades.observed_answer: No four-vote majority is needed. The player or players receiving the most votes are Targets, so Red is the sole Target with three votes versus two each for Blue and Green.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”
grades.reason: Applies highest count rather than absolute majority: Red alone is Target at three versus two and two.

grades.question: Red and Blue tie for the most votes. With neither playing Ambush, what happens to them, and may someone survive by having voted for either tied Target?
grades.expected_answer: Both tied Targets are eliminated. A non-Target voter who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and is not eliminated for voting outside the Target group.
grades.observed_answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player survives the voting requirement if they voted for either tied Target.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: all players tied for most votes are Targets; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”
grades.reason: Both tied Targets eliminated absent successful Ambush; vote for either Target satisfies the survival voting requirement.

grades.question: Blue is the sole Target. Green received no votes and voted for Red. Green did not Ambush. Does receiving no votes keep Green alive?
grades.expected_answer: No. A player who did not vote for a Target is also eliminated, even when nobody voted for that player. Green voted outside the Target group and is eliminated.
grades.observed_answer: No. Green is eliminated: every non-Target who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception. Green voted for Red rather than the sole Target, Blue, and did not Ambush.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated,” subject to successful Ambush.
grades.reason: Green is eliminated for voting outside the Target group despite receiving no votes.

grades.question: Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. How are votes tallied, who are the Targets, and who survives after Red's legal retaliation?
grades.expected_answer: Ambush adds no vote. Red and Yellow each have one vote and are tied Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives its successful Ambush and can retaliate only against Yellow, who voted for Red. Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.
grades.observed_answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count as one, so Red and Yellow tie for most votes and both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds; Red may eliminate a player who voted for Red, namely Yellow. Pink voted for a tied Target (Yellow), so Pink survives. Red and Pink survive.
grades.reader_evidence: The three-player illustration states Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes Red, and Pink votes Yellow; Red and Yellow tie as Targets, Red can retaliate only against Yellow, and Pink survives, leaving Red and Pink.
grades.reason: Complete vote tally ignoring Ambush, Red/Yellow tied Targets, Red protected/retaliates on Yellow, and Pink survives for voting TargetYellow.

grades.question: A Target successfully plays Ambush and four players voted for them. Do they eliminate all four voters? May they choose a player who voted for another color instead?
grades.expected_answer: The ambusher survives and eliminates exactly one of the players who voted for them. They neither eliminate every voter nor choose someone who did not vote for them.
grades.observed_answer: No. A successful Ambush lets its player choose one player who voted for them to eliminate; it does not eliminate all four voters. They cannot choose someone who voted for another color instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Ambush: a successful ambusher “chooses one of the players who voted for them” and cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.
grades.reason: Restricts successful Ambush retaliation to exactly one voter who targeted the ambusher; rejects all-voter and arbitrary-color alternatives.

grades.question: A player chooses Ambush but is not among the Targets after the votes are counted. What happens to that player?
grades.expected_answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
grades.observed_answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
grades.reader_evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”
grades.reason: Non-Target Ambush fails and self-eliminates.

grades.question: Four players survive a vote and its Ambush effects. Does the round award gold now, and who participates next?
grades.expected_answer: The round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the four survivors. It ends when the resolved vote leaves one, two or no survivors.
grades.observed_answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the survivors; only surviving players participate in subsequent votes.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: three or more survivors “continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”
grades.reason: Four survivors continue conspiracy/voting; no gold yet and only survivors vote.

grades.question: Exactly one player survives the round. What reward do they collect, and are the four cards four points?
grades.expected_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. Four bars are four cards, not four points; each Gold Bar is worth 3, 4 or 5 points.
grades.observed_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: one survivor collects all four central Gold Bars. Components: Gold Bars are cards, with values of 3, 4, or 5 points.
grades.reason: Sole survivor receives four central cards, each worth3/4/5points. No unsupported general publicity/reveal-timing claim.

grades.question: Exactly two players survive the voting. What must they do, which cards does each receive, and how do they choose and reveal?
grades.expected_answer: They must hold a Final Showdown. Each receives Share, Steal and Grab One & Go, may discuss intentions, secretly chooses one card face down, and reveals simultaneously with the other finalist.
grades.observed_answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; after any discussion or bargain, each chooses one card and places it face down. When both are ready, they reveal their choices simultaneously.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: each takes Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go, chooses one face down, and both reveal simultaneously when ready.
grades.reason: Explicit Share/Steal/Grab One & Go set, discussion, secret face-down selection and simultaneous reveal.

grades.question: The final vote eliminates every participant. Who receives gold from the deck, who does not, and what happens to the four central bars for next round?
grades.expected_answer: Nobody receives the central bars. Every player not involved in that final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; participants in that final vote receive none. Leave the four central bars and add no new central gold next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar, even if eliminated in it. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: with no survivors, each player not participating in the final vote gets one deck bar; leave the four central bars for next round and add no new bars. Special Rules clarifies final voters get no consolation bar.
grades.reason: Rewards only those absent from the final vote one deck card each; final voters receive none; all four central cards retained with no additions.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Share. How many Gold Bar cards does each receive?
grades.expected_answer: Each finalist receives two of the four central Gold Bar cards.
grades.observed_answer: Each receives two Gold Bar cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share against Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”
grades.reason: Share/Share yields two central cards each.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Share and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: The Share player receives no bars and the Steal player receives all four.
grades.observed_answer: The Share player receives zero cards and the Steal player receives all four central cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share against Steal: Share player gets 0; opponent gets 4.
grades.reason: Steal takes all four, Share takes zero.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Steal receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one card and the Steal player receives the other three central cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go against Steal gives the chooser 1 and the opponent 3; the rule says Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Steal three.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Share. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Share receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one card and the Share player receives the other three central cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go against Share gives the chooser 1 and the opponent 3; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Share three.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Grab One & Go. How many bars does each take, how many remain central, and how many new central bars are dealt if play continues?
grades.expected_answer: Each takes one central bar. Leave the other two central and deal just two new central bars for the next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. Two remain in the center, and if play continues add two new bars to bring the central pool back to four.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Grab One & Go, each gets one and the other two remain; add just two new bars for the next round.
grades.reason: Each takes one; two remain and only two new central cards dealt if continuing.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Steal. What do the finalists and the other players receive, and what happens to the central pot?
grades.expected_answer: Both finalists receive nothing. Each other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round rather than replacing them.
grades.observed_answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: double Steal means neither finalist gets gold; every other player gets one deck bar; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.
grades.reason: Finalists get zero, every other player one deck card; all four central cards retained without additions.

grades.question: When is victory checked, what totals win with 6–9 versus 10–12 players, and who wins if multiple players qualify with different totals?
grades.expected_answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.observed_answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded. The threshold is at least 25 points with 6–9 players and at least 24 points with 10–12 players. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: check “at the end of a round,” after awards; 25 points for 6–9 players, 24 for 10–12; if multiple qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.reason: Checks after awards at round end for every outcome; gives 25 for6–9,24 for10–12 and highest qualified total wins.

grades.question: At game end exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total. What does the booklet require? If a normal round ends without a winner, which eliminated players return?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
grades.observed_answer: The booklet's instruction, as summarized, is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. It does not provide a procedure or card arrangement for three or more tied leaders. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns for the next round, including players eliminated earlier; all Player IDs are stood upright again.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring says tied totals conduct another Final Showdown and repeat until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total; the source limitation says no arrangement is supplied for three or more. Turn Structure says everyone returns if there is no winner.
grades.reason: Exactly two tied qualified highest players hold further Showdowns until a single highest player exists; all players return with IDs upright if normal play continues.

grades.question: Before each vote, about how long should conspiracy last, may players communicate secretly or by texting/showing cards, and who asks for final decisions when it is time to vote?
grades.expected_answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
grades.observed_answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, or texting. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
grades.reader_evidence: Conspire: “roughly a minute and a half at most”; any method is allowed, including whispering, gestures, showing a Voting card, and texting; the game owner asks for final decisions.
grades.reason: Gives approximate90-second maximum before each vote, any overt/covert communication including requested examples, and game-owner final-decision call.

grades.question: When casting an ordinary vote rather than Ambush, which card do you choose and where do you put it? What card replaces that choice if you suspect you are the Target?
grades.expected_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
grades.observed_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the color of the player's visible ID and place it face down in front of yourself. If you want to defend yourself because you suspect you are the Target, play your own Ambush card instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: place one Voting card face down in front of yourself; target with the card matching that player's visible ID color; play your Ambush to defend yourself.
grades.reason: Names target-color Voting card, face-down placement in front of oneself, and own Ambush replacement; all requested parts explicit.

grades.question: After resolving a vote, how do the Player ID cards show who has been eliminated and who is eligible for the next vote?
grades.expected_answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
grades.observed_answer: Knock down the Player ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; they are eligible for the next vote.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”
grades.reason: Knocks eliminated IDs down and leaves survivors upright/eligible for next vote.

grades.question: A round awards all four central bars, either to a sole survivor or through a Showdown that distributes the entire pot. If nobody wins the game, how is the next central pool prepared?
grades.expected_answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
grades.observed_answer: If no one wins, keep any central bars left over and refill the pool to four by dealing only enough new bars to reach four, face down with values hidden. If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars.
grades.reader_evidence: After round rewards, refill to four as needed; bars left behind remain. Deal new bars face down; deal four if the pot was entirely awarded, otherwise add only enough to bring the pool to four.
grades.reason: Explicitly deals four new hidden-value/face-down bars after full pot distribution, refills only as necessary if leftovers; all requested preparation parts correct.

grades.question: In the illustrated vote with four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue plays a successful Ambush. Does Purple become the Target because Blue survives, and may voters for Purple survive on that basis?
grades.expected_answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
grades.observed_answer: No. Blue remains the sole Target with four votes versus Purple's three; Blue's successful Ambush lets Blue survive but does not change who the Target is. Voters for Purple did not vote for the Target, so they do not survive on that basis (absent a successful Ambush exception).
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: the player receiving the most votes is the Target; Ambush cards do not count as votes. Ambush: success protects its Target, and it “does not prevent another player from being a tied Target.” Vote: non-Targets who did not vote for any Target are eliminated, subject to successful Ambush.
grades.reason: Blue remains Target after successful Ambush; Purple not promoted; voters for Purple eliminated. Generic Ambush caveat is inapplicable to ordinary voters and supplies no actual alternate survival path.

grades.question: Three qualifying players are tied for the highest total at game end. What tie instruction does the booklet give, and does it specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two players?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
grades.observed_answer: The instruction is to have tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. The summary says the booklet does not specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two tied players; that procedure is unsupported.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: tied totals conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as necessary; source limitation: no arrangement for three or more players tied for highest qualifying total is supplied.
grades.reason: Independently adjudicated correct: full repeated-Showdown instruction and explicit absence of a multiway arrangement. Unsupported label describes the missing official procedure, exactly what the question asks about.

grades.question: During an extra Final Showdown between two players tied for the qualifying highest total, both Steal. Could a player outside that pair become the winner if the compensation bar gives that player the single highest total?
grades.expected_answer: Yes. Double Steal gives every player outside the pair one Gold Bar from the deck while the finalists get nothing. The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
grades.observed_answer: Yes, conditionally: if the outsider receives the compensation bar and thereby has the single highest total, the winner is the player with the highest point total, and the tie instruction seeks one player anywhere at the table with the highest total. The summary says double Steal awards every player other than the finalists one deck bar. It also notes the booklet does not specify how to supply the pot for extra game-end tie Showdowns, so whether that compensation applies in that extra showdown context is unsupported.
grades.reader_evidence: Double Steal: every other player gets one bar from the deck. Scoring: the highest point total wins and extra Showdowns repeat until one player anywhere at the table has the highest total. Source limitation: the pot for extra game-end tie Showdowns is unspecified.
grades.reason: Correct conditional opening, but final caveat explicitly leaves application of extra-Showdown deck compensation unsupported. This materially retracts the requested reward interaction. Independent adjudicator confirms partial; unlike readerB, it does not preserve the conditional ruling as resolved.

grades.question: When is victory checked, what totals win with 6–9 versus 10–12 players, and who wins if multiple players qualify with different totals?
grades.expected_answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.observed_answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after bars have been awarded. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: check at end of round after awards; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; highest point total wins.
grades.reason: Checks after awards at round end for every outcome; gives 25 for6–9,24 for10–12 and highest qualified total wins.

grades.question: At game end exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total. What does the booklet require? If a normal round ends without a winner, which eliminated players return?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
grades.observed_answer: The booklet's instruction, as summarized, is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown and repeat as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest gold point total. For exactly two tied players, that instruction is actionable using the two-player Showdown. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated earlier in the round; all IDs are stood upright for the next round.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeated as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total. Turn Structure: if no winner, everyone returns; stand all IDs upright.
grades.reason: Exactly two tied qualified highest players hold further Showdowns until a single highest player exists; all players return with IDs upright if normal play continues.

grades.question: Before each vote, about how long should conspiracy last, may players communicate secretly or by texting/showing cards, and who asks for final decisions when it is time to vote?
grades.expected_answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
grades.observed_answer: Before every vote, players conspire for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, including secretly, texting, and showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
grades.reader_evidence: Conspire: “for roughly a minute and a half at most”; communication may be open or secret, including texting and showing a Voting card; game owner asks for final decisions.
grades.reason: Gives approximate90-second maximum before each vote, any overt/covert communication including requested examples, and game-owner final-decision call.

grades.question: When casting an ordinary vote rather than Ambush, which card do you choose and where do you put it? What card replaces that choice if you suspect you are the Target?
grades.expected_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
grades.observed_answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the color of the target player's visible ID and place it face down in front of yourself. To defend yourself if you suspect you are the target, play your own Ambush card instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: place one card face down in front of yourself; target with the card matching that player's visible ID color; play Ambush to defend yourself.
grades.reason: Names target-color Voting card, face-down placement in front of oneself, and own Ambush replacement; all requested parts explicit.

grades.question: After resolving a vote, how do the Player ID cards show who has been eliminated and who is eligible for the next vote?
grades.expected_answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
grades.observed_answer: Knock down the Player ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; those survivors are the ones who participate in the next vote.
grades.reader_evidence: Resolve elimination: “Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.”
grades.reason: Knocks eliminated IDs down and leaves survivors upright/eligible for next vote.

grades.question: A round awards all four central bars, either to a sole survivor or through a Showdown that distributes the entire pot. If nobody wins the game, how is the next central pool prepared?
grades.expected_answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
grades.observed_answer: If no one wins, deal new central bars face down and keep their values hidden. Since the entire pot was awarded, deal four new bars to make the next central pool of four.
grades.reader_evidence: After round rewards: if the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars; deal new bars face down and keep values hidden.
grades.reason: Explicitly deals four new hidden-value/face-down bars after full pot distribution, refills only as necessary if leftovers; all requested preparation parts correct.

grades.question: In the illustrated vote with four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue plays a successful Ambush. Does Purple become the Target because Blue survives, and may voters for Purple survive on that basis?
grades.expected_answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
grades.observed_answer: No. Blue's successful Ambush does not make Purple a Target; the Target is determined by the vote count, and Ambush does not prevent another player from being a tied Target. With four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue is the sole Target. Voters for Purple do not survive on the basis of voting for Purple, since Purple is not a Target; they are outside the winning voting group and are eliminated, absent a successful Ambush of their own.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: most votes determines Target(s), and players outside the winning voting group are eliminated. Ambush: it “does not prevent another player from being a tied Target.”
grades.reason: Blue remains Target after successful Ambush; Purple not promoted; voters for Purple eliminated. Generic Ambush caveat is inapplicable to ordinary voters and supplies no actual alternate survival path.

grades.question: Three qualifying players are tied for the highest total at game end. What tie instruction does the booklet give, and does it specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two players?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
grades.observed_answer: The instruction is that tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown, repeating as necessary until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest point total. It does not specify how to arrange a Showdown among three or more players; the summary identifies this as requiring publisher clarification.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeat as necessary; the source limitation says the cards, procedure, and payoff cover only two players and supply no multiway procedure.
grades.reason: Accurately gives repeated Showdown requirement and explicitly identifies absence of a three-or-more-player arrangement; answers source-limitation question completely without inventing a solution.

grades.question: During an extra Final Showdown between two players tied for the qualifying highest total, both Steal. Could a player outside that pair become the winner if the compensation bar gives that player the single highest total?
grades.expected_answer: Yes. Double Steal gives every player outside the pair one Gold Bar from the deck while the finalists get nothing. The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
grades.observed_answer: Yes, if the compensation bar gives an outside player a point total that is uniquely highest, the stated end condition is a single player anywhere at the table having the highest total, so that player could be the winner. The summary says in a double-Steal every player other than the two finalists gets one deck bar. It does not specify how to supply the central pot for an extra game-end tie Showdown, but that limitation does not negate the stated possibility conditional on an outside player's total becoming uniquely highest.
grades.reader_evidence: Both Steal: every player other than the finalists receives one deck bar. Scoring: repeat Showdowns until a single player anywhere at the table has the highest total. Special Rules notes the pot for extra game-end tie Showdowns is unspecified.
grades.reason: Independently adjudicated correct: explicitly preserves conditional outsider-winning possibility, cites doubleSteal one-deck-bar reward and table-wide endpoint, and says pot uncertainty does not negate that conditional ruling. Reader support label partial is not grade.
